curriculum.title: 진단 범위, 데이터 흐름과 신뢰 경계

objectives.statement: 진단 대상과 입력·처리·출력의 신뢰 경계를 구분한다.
정적 분석에서 사실, 추론, 미확인 가정을 분리해 기록한다.
입력의 문법·범위·허용목록 검증과 해석기 경계를 설명한다.
명령·코드 해석으로 이어지는 데이터 흐름의 원인과 조치를 판정한다.
출력 컨텍스트와 프로토콜 경계에 맞는 안전한 처리 여부를 진단한다.
브라우저·응답·원격요청 관련 판단에서 확정 사실과 범위 밖 주장을 구분한다.
경로 정규화, 기준 디렉터리, 파일 형식 및 자원 수명 통제를 검토한다.
파일 처리 결과가 의도한 자원 경계를 벗어나지 않는지 검증 질문으로 표현한다.
오류 응답과 로그가 진단에 필요한 정보를 남기면서 민감한 내부정보를 노출하지 않는지 평가한다.
예외·실패·재시도 흐름의 관찰 가능성과 안전한 실패를 연결한다.
취약·안전·오탐 사례를 근거와 함께 구분하고 추가 확인사항을 제시한다.
조치가 원인·영향·검증 증거를 모두 다루는지 판단한다.

questions.purpose: Trace an unchecked identifier into a parser and name the missing allowlist/range check.
questions.stem: Review the request-to-parser flow. Is the diagnostic finding valid, and what evidence supports the verdict?

case.code: String mode = request.getParameter("mode"); Parser.parse(mode);
case.validationOrTransformation: none before parsing
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: Parser.parse interprets mode
assumptions: mode reaches this method without an upstream allowlist
Parser.parse interprets the supplied identifier

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: attacker-controlled parser input lacks an allowlist or range check

questions.vulnerabilityReason: Attacker-controlled parser input is interpreted without a grammar, allowlist, or range control.
questions.explanation: The source is attacker-controlled and flows directly into an interpreting parser. Because no grammar, allowlist, or range control is shown, a crafted identifier can select an unintended parse path. Cite the request source, absent validation, and parser sink.

questions.purpose: Confirm grammar, range, canonical form, and rejection behavior before interpretation.
questions.stem: Review the same parser boundary after the proposed control. Is the finding resolved, and what residual limitation remains?

case.code: String raw = request.getParameter("mode"); Mode mode = Mode.fromAllowlist(raw); if (mode == null) reject(); Parser.parse(mode.token());
case.validationOrTransformation: strict closed allowlist maps input to a known token and rejects unknown values
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: Parser.parse receives only the allowlisted token
assumptions: Mode.fromAllowlist has no fallback that accepts arbitrary input
reject stops processing

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the allowlist breaks the attacker-controlled identifier flow

questions.mitigationReason: The closed allowlist and rejecting branch prevent arbitrary request text from reaching the parser.
questions.explanation: The request remains untrusted, but unknown values are rejected and accepted values are converted to a closed set before parsing. The control breaks arbitrary input flow at validation; the residual limitation is that the allowlist must remain complete and correctly maintained.

questions.purpose: Recognize a flagged concatenation whose value is a closed compile-time allowlist and document the evidence needed.
questions.stem: A rule flags a value assembled before parsing. Decide whether the alert is exploitable under the stated call-site facts.

case.code: static final String DEFAULT_MODE = "READ_ONLY"; String mode = "" + DEFAULT_MODE; Parser.parse(mode);
case.source: no request, file, environment, or user input reaches mode
case.validationOrTransformation: compile-time constant concatenation; no dynamic value
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: Parser.parse interprets a fixed token
assumptions: DEFAULT_MODE is final and initialized only to the shown literal
the shown method has no alternate caller-supplied mode

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the suspicious concatenation cannot carry attacker data under the stated call-site facts

questions.nonExploitabilityReason: The parser input is a closed compile-time constant and the call site has no external selector, so attacker data cannot reach the sink under the stated facts.
questions.explanation: The pattern resembles an input-to-parser flow, but the value is a closed compile-time constant and there is no external source. The alert is non-exploitable only if the final constant and call-site closure are verified; cite those facts rather than trusting a label.

questions.purpose: Identify user-controlled data crossing an operating-system command interpreter boundary.
questions.stem: Review the command construction and determine whether the analyzer finding represents command injection.

case.code: String name = request.getParameter("name"); new ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", "convert " + name).start();
case.validationOrTransformation: string concatenation; no command or argument allowlist
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: shell interpreter executes the constructed command
assumptions: the process is reachable from the request handler
the service account can start the process

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: attacker data reaches a shell command string

questions.explanation: The request value is concatenated into a string interpreted by a shell. Metacharacters can change the command grammar, so the missing control is not merely input cleaning: the shell boundary itself is unsafe. Cite the source, concatenation, and interpreter sink.

questions.purpose: Select a fixed operation plus argument-array API and least-privilege execution boundary.
questions.stem: Compare the argument-array version with the vulnerable shell version. Is the command-injection finding resolved?

case.code: String name = request.getParameter("name"); String safe = NameAllowlist.require(name); new ProcessBuilder("convert", safe).start();
case.validationOrTransformation: strict name allowlist; ProcessBuilder receives separate arguments and no shell
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: fixed executable receives one argument
assumptions: NameAllowlist rejects separators and unsupported names
convert is resolved to the fixed approved executable
the process uses least privilege

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: allowlisting plus an argument-array API removes shell interpretation

questions.explanation: The input is still attacker-controlled, but it is constrained and passed as a separate argument to a fixed executable. No shell parses the value, so shell metacharacters do not become command syntax. Residual risk is limited to the correctness of executable resolution and allowlist policy.

questions.purpose: Reject an alert where the invoked operation and every argument are fixed constants, subject to call-site evidence.
questions.stem: A rule flags shell execution. Decide whether the shown call is exploitable under the deployment and reachability assumptions.

case.code: static final String CHECK = "convert --version"; new ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", CHECK).start();
case.source: the command string is a compile-time constant in a test-only health fixture
case.validationOrTransformation: no external value is concatenated or read
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: shell interpreter receives a fixed constant command
assumptions: the fixture is not shipped on a request-reachable production path
CHECK and every call argument are immutable constants
no environment substitution occurs

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the shell pattern is suspicious but no attacker-controlled command data reaches it

questions.nonExploitabilityReason: The shell receives only an immutable constant in a non-production fixture, so attacker-controlled command data cannot reach the sink under the stated call-site and packaging facts.
questions.explanation: Shell execution is a valid suspicious sink, but this call has a fixed command and no external source under the stated reachability facts. It is not a blanket safe pattern: the reviewer must verify the constant, call graph, packaging, and absence of environment interpolation.

questions.purpose: Trace data from a request into a dynamic evaluator and identify the interpreter boundary.
questions.stem: Determine whether request data can become executable code at the evaluator boundary.

case.code: String expression = request.getParameter("expression"); evaluator.eval(expression);
case.validationOrTransformation: none; raw expression is forwarded
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: dynamic evaluator executes the expression
assumptions: evaluator.eval accepts general expressions
the handler is reachable by an attacker

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: attacker-controlled text reaches a code interpreter

questions.explanation: The request supplies the evaluator program rather than only data for a fixed operation. Because there is no typed command model or constrained grammar, attacker input can alter executable behavior. Cite the request source and dynamic evaluator sink.

questions.purpose: Choose a typed operation model that removes dynamic evaluation and constrains inputs.
questions.stem: Does replacing dynamic evaluation with a typed operation dispatch mitigate the code-injection finding?

case.code: String operation = request.getParameter("operation"); switch (Operation.allowlist(operation)) { case ADD -> add(); case SUBTRACT -> subtract(); default -> reject(); }
case.validationOrTransformation: closed operation allowlist maps to typed branches
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: fixed application methods; no evaluator
assumptions: Operation.allowlist returns no arbitrary method or code reference
default rejects unknown values

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the request selects data-independent typed behavior rather than code

questions.explanation: The request can select one of two known operations, but it cannot supply a program. The evaluator sink is removed and unknown operations are rejected. The control is valid only if the dispatch table remains closed and does not reintroduce reflection or dynamic evaluation.

questions.purpose: Distinguish a static analyzer hit on a test-only fixed expression from a reachable user-data path.
questions.stem: A dynamic-evaluation API is present in a test fixture. Decide whether this is a code-injection vulnerability in the stated build.

case.code: static final String FIXTURE = "1 + 1"; evaluator.eval(FIXTURE);
case.source: FIXTURE is a compile-time constant in a non-packaged unit test
case.validationOrTransformation: no request or configuration value reaches FIXTURE
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: dynamic evaluator executes a fixed test expression
assumptions: the test class is excluded from the deployable artifact
FIXTURE cannot be overridden by reflection or environment data

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the evaluator is a suspicious sink but the tested expression is fixed and unreachable in production

questions.nonExploitabilityReason: The evaluator receives a compile-time constant from a test class excluded from deployment, so no attacker-controlled program can reach this sink in the stated build.
questions.explanation: The API resembles the vulnerable case, but no attacker-controlled source reaches it and the class is excluded from production. The verdict depends on build and call-site evidence; if either assumption fails, the alert becomes a real vulnerability.

questions.purpose: Determine whether a requested file can escape the intended base directory after normalization.
questions.stem: Review the file lookup and determine whether the requested name can escape the configured document root.

case.code: Path base = Paths.get("/srv/docs"); Path file = base.resolve(request.getParameter("name")).normalize(); Files.readString(file);
case.validationOrTransformation: normalize removes lexical dot segments but no base-containment check follows
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: file read at the resolved path
assumptions: the process can read files outside /srv/docs
no authorization or symlink policy is applied elsewhere

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: normalized attacker-selected path is not proven contained by the base

questions.explanation: Normalization alone does not establish containment. A relative traversal or absolute path can resolve outside the intended base, and the subsequent file read uses that result without a confinement check. Cite source, incomplete validation, and file-read sink.

questions.purpose: Verify canonicalization, base confinement, safe file identity, and authorization together.
questions.stem: Does the containment check make this file lookup safe under the stated filesystem assumptions?

case.code: Path base = Paths.get("/srv/docs").toRealPath(); String key = ResourceKey.allowlist(request.getParameter("name")); Path file = base.resolve(key).normalize(); if (!file.startsWith(base)) reject(); Files.readString(file);
case.validationOrTransformation: closed key allowlist, canonical base, normalization, and explicit base containment
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: file read only after containment and authorization checks
assumptions: ResourceKey rejects separators and maps only approved resources
base and file resolution use the same filesystem view
the caller is authorized for the selected resource

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the closed key and containment guard block escape from the canonical base

questions.explanation: The request is untrusted, but it is reduced to a closed resource key and the normalized result must remain under the canonical base before reading. Authorization is also stated as a precondition. Residual limitations include filesystem changes after resolution and the correctness of the key map.

questions.purpose: Recognize a safe path join when the identifier is an enum-backed resource key rather than a path fragment.
questions.stem: A rule flags a path join followed by a read. Is the alert valid when the key and mapping are closed as described?

case.code: Path base = Paths.get("/srv/docs").toRealPath(); Path file = base.resolve(ResourceKey.HELP.path()).normalize(); Files.readString(file);
case.source: ResourceKey.HELP is a fixed enum member; no request value reaches path()
case.validationOrTransformation: enum-backed closed resource mapping; no dynamic path fragment
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: file read under the fixed application base
assumptions: every ResourceKey path is a fixed relative constant without separators that escape the base
the enum cannot be selected by unvalidated external input at this call site
the base is the intended resource root

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the flagged join has no attacker-controlled path component under the closed enum facts

questions.nonExploitabilityReason: The joined path component is a fixed enum value proven relative to the intended base, and no external selector reaches this call site, so traversal data cannot enter the read.
questions.explanation: The API shape resembles a traversal sink, but the path component is a fixed enum mapping and the call site has no external selector. The finding is non-exploitable only after verifying the enum values, call graph, and base root; otherwise the same pattern must be reclassified.

questions.purpose: Evaluate a file upload that trusts client metadata and stores content in a served location.
questions.stem: Does this upload handler safely control the file identity and storage boundary?

case.code: String filename = part.getSubmittedFileName(); part.write(Paths.get("/srv/www/uploads").resolve(filename));
case.source: multipart filename and bytes are attacker-controlled
case.validationOrTransformation: client filename is used directly; no independent type, size, name, or storage policy
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: write into a web-served directory
assumptions: the upload endpoint is reachable by an attacker
the served directory can expose or execute selected files

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: attacker-controlled metadata selects a served storage path

questions.explanation: The client controls both content and the filename used to form the destination. The handler lacks independent content checks, generated identity, size limits, and a non-served storage boundary, so an uploaded object can cross the application’s file-serving or execution boundary.

questions.purpose: Select independent content checks, generated names, non-served storage, size limits, and malware review hooks.
questions.stem: Does the repaired upload flow prevent client metadata from controlling a served executable path?

case.code: UploadMeta meta = UploadPolicy.inspect(part, 5_000_000); String id = IdGenerator.randomId(); Path target = privateStore.resolve(id); privateStore.write(target, meta.bytes()); malwareReview.enqueue(target);
case.source: multipart filename and bytes are attacker-controlled
case.validationOrTransformation: independent type/content and size checks; generated opaque name; private storage; review hook
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: write to non-served private storage after policy checks
assumptions: UploadPolicy does not trust the client MIME or extension alone
privateStore is not web-served or executable
review failure prevents publication

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: independent policy and private generated storage break the unsafe upload path

questions.explanation: The client still supplies bytes, but client metadata no longer chooses the identity or serving location. Independent checks, limits, generated names, private storage, and review controls address the relevant handling risks. Residual safety depends on the private-store and publication assumptions.

questions.purpose: Clear an alert for a fixed internal fixture only when reachability and deployment evidence exclude external input.
questions.stem: A file-copy rule flags a fixture import. Is it a real upload vulnerability under the stated build and reachability facts?

case.code: Path fixture = TEST_FIXTURE_ROOT.resolve("avatar.png"); Files.copy(fixture, PRIVATE_REVIEW_DIR.resolve("fixture-avatar"));
case.source: fixture path and destination name are fixed test constants
case.validationOrTransformation: no multipart or user-selected filename; test-only fixture source
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: copy into a private review directory
assumptions: TEST_FIXTURE_ROOT contains repository-controlled test data
the test class is excluded from production and no user controls the constants
PRIVATE_REVIEW_DIR is not served or executable

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the file operation resembles upload handling but has no external source or served destination

questions.nonExploitabilityReason: Both path components are fixed repository-controlled test constants, the test is not deployed, and the destination is private; no attacker-controlled upload reaches this copy.
questions.explanation: A superficial rule sees a file copy, but the source and destination are fixed internal test resources and no multipart input reaches the operation. The reviewer must verify packaging, constants, and destination policy; if any becomes user-controlled, the verdict changes.

questions.purpose: Match the output context to the missing contextual encoding or safe rendering control.
questions.stem: Is the response construction vulnerable to script injection in the HTML text context?

case.code:
String q = request.getParameter("q"); response.getWriter().write("
" + q + "
");
case.validationOrTransformation: none; raw value is concatenated into HTML
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: HTML response writer in a browser-rendered context
assumptions: the response is interpreted as HTML
q is not encoded by an outer template layer

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: attacker-controlled text reaches an HTML sink without contextual encoding

questions.explanation: The browser interprets the response as HTML and the query value is inserted raw. A payload can change the document context because no HTML-text encoding or safe text renderer intervenes. Cite the source, response context, and missing control.

questions.purpose: Verify context-specific encoding, safe templating, and appropriate browser policy as layered controls.
questions.stem: Does the context-aware text renderer mitigate the HTML injection finding while preserving visible user text?

case.code:
String q = request.getParameter("q"); response.getWriter().write("
" + HtmlEncoder.forText(q) + "
");
case.validationOrTransformation: HTML-text-context encoding immediately before output
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: HTML response writer receives encoded text
assumptions: HtmlEncoder.forText is the approved encoder for this exact HTML text context
q is not later inserted into an attribute, script, or URL context

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: context-appropriate encoding prevents the value from becoming HTML markup

questions.explanation: The same attacker-controlled value is rendered, but the encoder transforms markup-significant characters for the exact text context before the response sink. The control does not authorize reuse in another context; the stated residual limitation is context fidelity.

questions.purpose: Identify a value rendered only as text by a verified safe renderer rather than an executable markup context.
questions.stem: A rule flags user text reaching a response writer. Is the finding valid when the renderer contract is proven?

case.code: String label = request.getParameter("label"); response.getWriter().write(TextRenderer.textNode(label));
case.validationOrTransformation: TextRenderer.textNode performs context-locked HTML text encoding and cannot emit markup
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: HTML response writer receives a text node representation
assumptions: TextRenderer.textNode is the reviewed context-aware text API
the returned value is not decoded or reinterpreted later
the output remains in an HTML text context

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the suspicious source-to-writer flow is non-exploitable because the reviewed renderer enforces text context

questions.nonExploitabilityReason: The attacker-controlled label is encoded by a reviewed text-only renderer and cannot become markup in the final HTML text context under the stated contract.
questions.explanation: Unlike the vulnerable raw concatenation, the value is passed through a renderer whose contract is specifically to produce text, not markup. The reviewer must prove the renderer implementation and final context; the conclusion is not based on the variable name or a falsePositive flag.

questions.purpose: Identify internal paths, identifiers, or stack details disclosed through a user-facing error response.
questions.stem: Does this error path disclose sensitive diagnostic details to the requester?

case.code: try { loadConfig(); } catch (Exception e) { response.sendError(500, e.getMessage()); logger.error("load failed", e); }
case.source: exception data may contain filesystem paths, identifiers, or configuration details
case.validationOrTransformation: none before user-facing error response
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: HTTP error body and diagnostic log
assumptions: e.getMessage can contain internal detail
the response is visible to the requester
logger output is protected but the response is not

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: internal exception detail is copied into a user-facing response

questions.explanation: The exception is a security-relevant source of internal detail and its message flows directly to the requester. Logging the exception may be appropriate, but returning the same data discloses implementation and environment information. Cite the exception source and response sink.

questions.purpose: Separate correlation-safe user errors from protected diagnostic logs with access and retention controls.
questions.stem: Does this revised error path preserve useful diagnosis without disclosing internal exception details?

case.code: try { loadConfig(); } catch (Exception e) { String id = Correlation.newId(); response.sendError(500, "Request failed; reference " + id); secureLogger.error(id, e); }
case.source: exception data remains security-relevant and attacker-influenced through the failing request
case.validationOrTransformation: user response is fixed plus opaque correlation ID; detail stays in protected log
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: bounded HTTP error and access-controlled diagnostic log
assumptions: the correlation ID contains no secret or stack detail
secureLogger access and retention are restricted
the client cannot query raw logs

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the response/log boundary separates user-safe information from protected diagnostics

questions.explanation: The application still records the exception for diagnosis, but the requester receives only a bounded message and opaque reference. The exact safety control is separation of sinks plus protected log access; residual risk is misconfigured logging or correlation data.

questions.purpose: Treat a deliberately redacted error as non-exposing only after confirming the redaction boundary and log permissions.
questions.stem: A rule flags exception handling near an error response. Is the alert valid when the response is a fixed redacted message?

case.code: try { loadConfig(); } catch (Exception e) { response.sendError(400, REDACTED_REQUEST_MESSAGE); secureLogger.info("invalid request"); }
case.source: exception is caught, but no exception value is copied into the response or log message
case.validationOrTransformation: fixed redacted message and fixed log event
case.sinkOrSensitiveOperation: HTTP error and protected constant log event
assumptions: REDACTED_REQUEST_MESSAGE is a fixed non-sensitive constant
the logger call does not include e, request data, or stack details
the response is not decorated by middleware with the exception

answerKey.diagnosticConclusion: the exception-handling shape is suspicious but no sensitive exception data reaches either sink

questions.nonExploitabilityReason: The catch block discards the exception and emits only fixed redacted content to both sinks, so internal exception data cannot reach the requester or log under the middleware assumptions.
questions.explanation: The catch block can trigger a rule because it handles an exception near a response, but the shown data flow discards the exception and emits only fixed, redacted content. The reviewer must verify middleware and logger behavior; if either adds exception data, the finding is no longer false positive.
